# dsh-desktop-restart-button
English | 中文

A **restart button** for **DeepSeek Harness Desktop on Windows**, plus a small
tech-style boot anima

tion that replaces the app's plain "Loading settings…"
cold-start caption.

Both are drawn by an inline index-injection row, so **`app.asar` is never
touched** — installing and

uninstalling this plugin leaves the shipped
application exactly as it was.
## Why a plugin and not a menu item

The desktop window menu bar (`应用` / `编辑`) is built by Electron's preload
script with exactly two har

d-coded buttons, and the app exposes **no restart IPC
channel and no CLI entry point** — its own `ap

p.relaunch()` menu item only exists
in development builds. There is also no way to use `dsh plugin -

-profile desktop`,
because the desktop profile is managed exclusively by the Electron application.

The one supported extension point on the desktop is a **profile plugin that
pushes an inline script

row into the host's index injection table**. That is what
this package is.
## Install

Desktop profiles cannot be managed from the CLI. Install it through the app's
own plugin manager:

1. Open **设置 → 插件** in the app.
2. Search for `dsh-desktop-restart-button` (or install from a local

tarball).
3. Restart the app once.

The button appears in the title bar, right after `应用` and `编辑`. On any
platform other than Windows t

he plugin loads but adds nothing: the menu bar it
attaches to only exists on Windows, and the restar
t path is WMI/PowerShell.
## Why restarting needs a launcher at all

Electron puts children of the app into a **Job Object**, and every process the
app spawns is killed

when the app is killed. A restarter started the normal way
would therefore kill the app and then die

with it, leaving the user staring at a
closed window. `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` is refused by tha

it, leaving the user staring at a
closed window. `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` is refused by that job.
The chain that works, and the one this plugin uses:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`wscript.exe` is not an accident: WMI-created `powershell.exe` always flashes a
console window, and

neither `-WindowStyle Hidden` nor
`Win32_ProcessStartup.ShowWindow = 0` suppresses it (while
`Create

Flags = CREATE_NO_WINDOW` makes the WMI call fail outright). A
GUI-subsystem binary plus `WshShell.R

un(cmd, 0, False)` is the only combination
that stays invisible.

Measured on the author's machine: **click → window back ≈ 5 seconds**, most of
which is Host startup
, not the restart itself.
## Safety

- **Origin fence.** The restart route accepts only `dsh-app://app` (how the
desktop shell serves its

own UI) and loopback origins. A random web page in
your browser cannot reach it.
- **In-job guard.*

* `restart.ps1` calls `IsProcessInJob` before touching
anything. If it finds itself inside the app's

job — for example because
someone ran it by hand from a terminal that the app owns — it re-dispatch

es
itself through the WMI launcher and exits **without killing the app**,
instead of closing it and

dying.
- **No data is lost on purpose.** The app is asked to close its window first
and is only forc

e-killed if it is still alive afterwards, so settings and
session writes finish normally.
- **Never

leaves a closed app.** If the relaunch does not take, the restarter
retries for up to a minute befor

sed app.** If the relaunch does not take, the restarter
retries for up to a minute before giving up.
Log: `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\dsh-desktop-restart-button.log`
## Configuration
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`bootAnimation` defaults to `true`. Set it to `false` to keep the app's original
"正在加载设置…" caption.

Requires an app restart to take effect, since the
injection row is collected once at startup.
## The boot animation

The overlay it replaces is the app's onboarding surface, which renders a lone
`[role="status"]` node

while the Host is starting. The plugin marks **only that
exact state** (an overlay that has a statu

s node and no wizard content) and
hides the caption on the marked element via an attribute selector

— the real
onboarding wizard keeps its own text.

The animation itself is pure CSS/SVG (three counter-rotating arcs, a breathing
core, a sweeping bar,

a slowly drifting dot grid) with a
`prefers-reduced-motion` fallback to static. No canvas, no rAF l

oop, no work
after the overlay unmounts.
## Notes and limits

- **Windows only.** `dsh.bundle.platforms: ["win32"]`.
- **Desktop only.** It attaches to the preloa

d-built window menu bar, which a
plain `dsh web` session does not have. On web the plugin is harmles

s but
invisible.
- The app relaunches `process.execPath`, i.e. the executable the host is
running as

. If that is ever not the desktop binary, it falls back to
`D:\deepseek\DeepSeek Harness.exe`.
- The

desktop host binds a **random port every start**, so the page you were on
is not valid after a rest
art. The button does not try to navigate for you.
